title: Sell Mineral Rights in Cody, WY
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Cody, WY | Park County
metaDescription: Cody, WY sits over Bighorn Basin legacy oil ground, Oregon Basin and Garland fields, alongside its Yellowstone gateway economy. Get an honest mineral read.
heroLead: Cody markets itself as the gateway to Yellowstone, but under the tourism economy sits Park County oil history that goes back over a hundred years, the Oregon Basin and Garland fields among them.
intro: Oregon Basin, discovered in the early 1900s, became one of the larger fields in the Bighorn Basin, and Garland field to the north has its own long production history. Both have seen decades of secondary recovery work to keep producing well past what primary drilling alone would have delivered. Park County recorder records around Cody reflect that century of activity, layered lease filings, unit agreements, and multi-generation probate transfers.

If your family's mineral interest is tied to this area, whether from an old homestead or a more recent purchase, I check your specific tract against these known field boundaries before I say anything about what it's worth.

sections.heading: Oregon Basin and Garland, a century apart from discovery
paragraphs: Both fields have gone through the typical lifecycle of a mature Wyoming asset, strong primary production followed by declining pressure, then waterflood or other enhanced-recovery investment to sustain output. That kind of sustained capital commitment from operators tells me there's still recoverable oil in place, which is relevant to how much runway a producing interest here might have left.
Decline on assets this mature tends to be gradual rather than steep, a different value profile than a new horizontal well elsewhere in the state.

sections.heading: Tourism economy, separate mineral story
paragraphs: Cody's growth as a Yellowstone gateway town has driven up surface real estate values in recent decades, but that has essentially no bearing on mineral value, which is priced on geology, lease history, and production data, not on tourism traffic or hotel occupancy. I keep those two conversations separate when I talk to owners here.

sections.heading: Confirming your ownership
paragraphs: I pull the Park County recorder's chain of title for your specific section and check current well and unit status through state records before quoting anything, so the number reflects your actual position, not a countywide average.

faqs.question: Are Oregon Basin and Garland still producing?
faqs.answer: Portions of both remain active under enhanced recovery. I'll check your specific tract's current status.

faqs.question: Does Cody's tourism growth affect my mineral value?
faqs.answer: Not directly. Mineral value is driven by geology and production history, not surface real estate trends.

faqs.question: My deed references an old homestead name, not a legal description. Can you still help?
faqs.answer: Usually, yes. I can often match a homestead or ranch name to a legal description through Park County records.

faqs.question: What if my interest has never produced?
faqs.answer: I'll price it as undeveloped acreage, distinct from the producing interests tied to the historic fields.
